learn.title: Many values, one name
learn.body: An array holds several values of the same type, one after another in memory. Instead of `score1`, `score2` and `score3` you write one name and pick a position. Arrays make loops over data possible.

learn.title: Declaring an array
learn.body: `int scores[3];` makes room for three ints. The number in brackets is the length. You can fill it at the same time: `int scores[3] = {90, 75, 60};`. Leave the brackets empty and the compiler counts for you: `int a[] = {4, 8, 15};`.

learn.title: Indexing starts at 0
learn.body: The first element is `scores[0]`, the last is `scores[2]`. An element can be read and also changed with `=`.

learn.title: Why zero
learn.body: An index counts how far an element sits from the start. The first one is 0 steps away. So an array of length 3 has indexes 0, 1 and 2, and the last valid index is always length minus 1.

learn.title: Fewer values than slots
learn.body: With `int a[5] = {1, 2};` the other slots become 0, so printing all five shows 1 2 0 0 0. Without braces a local array holds unpredictable leftovers, so always initialize.

learn.title: How long is it
learn.body: `sizeof a` is the size in bytes. Dividing by the size of one element gives the length. Here 16 bytes divided by 4 bytes is 4.
For an array of length n, the last element is `a[n - 1]`, not `a[n]`.

questions.prompt: What is the index of the first element of an array?
questions.explanation: Indexes count steps from the start, so the first element is 0 steps away.

questions.prompt: In `int a[10];`, what is the largest valid index? Type the number.

questions.explanation: The compiler counts the values in the braces.

questions.prompt: After `int a[5] = {1, 2};`, what is `a[4]`? Type the number.
questions.explanation: Slots without a value in the braces are set to 0.

questions.prompt: An array of 6 ints holds \_\_ bytes, if an int is 4 bytes.
questions.explanation: 6 times 4 is 24, which is `sizeof` of the whole array.

questions.prompt: Which expression gives the number of elements of `int v[]`?
questions.explanation: Total bytes divided by the bytes of one element.
An assignment replaces the stored value.

questions.prompt: Match each expression to its meaning for `int a[4]`.
questions.explanation: Valid indexes are 0 to 3, and four ints take 16 bytes.
